pr.title: feat(about): SD card size, used and free space
pr.body:
## Summary

* **Goal:** see how full the SD card is without a computer.
* **What changes:** Settings → System → About gets three rows under Flash — **SD Size**, **SD Used**, **SD Free** (GB with one decimal, MB below 1 GB).
  * The used space comes from the SDK's FAT scan (`SDCardManager::sdUsedBytes`, cached by the SDK), which takes a few seconds on a large card, so a **Loading** popup answers the press before the scan.
  * Labels stay hardcoded English, like the rest of About, for support screenshots.
  * `HalStorage` gets two thin wrappers (`sdTotalBytes`, `sdUsedBytes`) that take the storage lock, like its other calls.

![Settings → System → About, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MikalaiKryvusha/crosspoint-reader/pr-assets/04-about-sd/about-sd-card.png)

*Simulator; it has no SD volume, so the values in the screenshot are the host disk's.*

## Scope Check

- [x] I have read SCOPE.md and ROADMAP.md.
- [x] This PR is **not** a new built-in theme.
- [x] This PR is **not** a new external network connector.
- [x] This PR is **not** an interactive app, writing tool, RSS/news/browser, media playback, or PDF feature.
- [x] The stock firmware does not already handle this well, **and** no other popular CrossPoint fork already does.
- [ ] This PR touches `lib/hal/` — two read-only `HalStorage` wrappers over existing SDK calls; happy to adjust to whatever the HAL owner prefers.

## Additional Context

* `pio run -e x4pro` is green (flash +~1 KB).
* The rows and the Loading popup run on my X4 Pro build.

---

### AI Usage

Did you use AI tools to help write this code? _**YES**_ — Claude (Anthropic) wrote the change under my direction; I reviewed it.

I cant see the freeink changes on the main branch.

Also, 
> "No card" when nothing is mounted

is redundent, since the reader wont let you access the settings (or anything else) if no card is presented.

Thanks, @Uri-Tauber — both points are right.

- **SDK:** the `sdUsedBytes()` change is now its own PR: Free-Ink/freeink-sdk#181. This PR will point the submodule at it once it is merged.
- **No card:** instead of dropping the row, the device now boots without a card. Settings keep their defaults and are not saved, the library is empty, and About shows "No card". Before this change it stopped on "SD card error". Recovery mode (Down + Power) still needs a card; without one the device boots normally.

Checked in the simulator with storage made to fail (a local patch to the simulator): boot, Settings → System → About, a setting toggle, Back to Home, Browse Files ("No files found"), sleep and wake. With a card nothing changes. `x4pro` and `default` build, 893 host tests pass.

@Uri-Tauber, a heads-up: I can't open any new PR here right now, not even a draft. GitHub refuses with a permissions error. I have five PRs open, so I guess it is the per-user open-PR limit and it is set to 5.

Four more are ready: Screen Cleaning submenu, screen calibration, delayed image redraws, Home / control-center cleaning. If you want the project to grow, 5 feels low for active contributors. Could you raise it?

> No card: instead of dropping the row, the device now boots without a card. Settings keep their defaults and are not saved, the library is empty, and About shows "No card". Before this change it stopped on "SD card error". Recovery mode (Down + Power) still needs a card; without one the device boots normally.

I'm against this change. It has its reasons.

> Four more are ready: Screen Cleaning submenu, screen calibration, delayed image redraws, Home / control-center cleaning. If you want the project to grow, 5 feels low for active contributors. Could you raise it?

IT was intentional. A relatively-new restriction after new contributors opened dozens of AI-generated PRs without even verifying on actual device. I fear it also apply to you, as your description says you only tested in the simulator. Do you have an actual device?

Yes, I have a real X4 Pro, and I run tests on it constantly — this is the second day.

On the card: agreed, I'm reverting the no-card boot.
Done: the no-card boot is reverted, and the "No card" state is gone from About.

@Uri-Tauber, on real-device testing, have a look at KEINKT: https://mikalaikryvusha.github.io/KEINKT/calibrator/ (source: https://github.com/MikalaiKryvusha/KEINKT). It measures my X4 Pro's panel from phone photos of calibration targets and builds the tone curves for the calibration PR. A tool like that can't be written without a real device in hand.

I'd also ask you to reconsider the blanket bias against AI tools. What matters is whether the author checks the work on a real device, not which tools helped write it.
To be clear: if the bias and the dismissive tone continue, I'll stop contributing to CrossPoint and keep developing my own fork.

> I'd also ask you to reconsider the blanket bias against AI tools. What matters is whether the author checks the work on a real device, not which tools helped write it.

I dont have any bias against AI tolls, I use them myself heavily. What I do want is accountability. If you contribute code you should understand what it does, how it does it and why it does it. It's more than just checking everything seems to work on the surface. 

> To be clear: if the bias and the dismissive tone continue, I'll stop contributing to CrossPoint and keep developing my own fork.

I'm sorry if my tone was too harsh. It wasn't intended.
I merged your SDK PR. Update the submodule pointer.

**Report unavailable SD usage instead of zero.** `sdUsedBytes()` returns 0 in two cases: when the card is not initialized, and when a FAT scan returns a negative free-cluster count. The scan-failure zero is cached until the cache expires. `sdTotalBytes()` returns the cached total without checking the mount state. If the card is removed, or a scan fails, after the total query returns a nonzero value, About can show SD Used as zero and SD Free as the full capacity. The `sdTotal == 0` check does not detect this. The SDK API has no error channel, so `AboutActivity` alone cannot distinguish a failure from a real zero. The fix needs a failure signal from `sdUsedBytes()` in the SDK submodule, passed through `HalStorage`. When that signal is set, show `-` for SD Used and SD Free, as the existing `No card` branch does.
